q: Work must be done to separate two bodies having opposite charges since they attract each other.
e: True. Work must be done to separate two bodies having opposite charges since they attract each other. Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts.

q: Work must be done to bring closer two bodies having the same kind of charge since they repel each other.
e: True. Work must be done to bring closer two bodies having the same kind of charge since they repel each other. Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts.

q: In both cases the work done is stored up in the charged objects as electric kinetic energy.
e: False. Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion. The written line says In both cases the work done is stored up in the charged objects as electric kinetic energy.

q: The work done in bringing the charge $q$ against the electric force from infinity to a point in an electric field is the electric potential energy of charge $q$ at that point.
e: True. The work done in bringing the charge q against the electric force from infinity to a point in an electric field is the electric potential energy of charge q at that point. Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q.

q: The electric potential at a point in an electric field is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge against the electric force from infinity to that point.
e: True. The electric potential at a point in an electric field is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge against the electric force from infinity to that point. Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q.

q: The electric potential at a point can be expressed as $V = \frac{W}{q}$.
e: True. The electric potential at a point can be expressed as V = (W)/(q). Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q.

q: The practical unit of electric potential is the volt (V).
e: True. The practical unit of electric potential is the volt (V). Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q.

q: If the work done in bringing +1 coulomb from infinity to a point in an electric field is 1 joule, the electric potential at that point is 1 volt.
e: True. If the work done in bringing +1 coulomb from infinity to a point in an electric field is 1 joule, the electric potential at that point is 1 volt. Coulomb's law: F = K q1 q2 / r². Like charges repel; unlike charges attract.

q: The electric potential difference between two points in an electric field is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge from one point to another against electric force.
e: True. The electric potential difference between two points in an electric field is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge from one point to another against electric force. Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q.

q: A positive charge will move from a point of lower electric potential to a point of higher electric potential.
e: False. The claim puts positive where negative belongs. A negative charge will move from a point of lower electric potential to a point of higher electric potential. Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q.
